title: Tree-wide checks evaluate before any scope short-circuit
context: DEFINE step 3 rulings R2 (draftSettled tree-wide), R5 (entityJoin unconditional) and R7 (standardsCited tree-wide) landed on the same shape: a stage whose scope narrows to nothing (D3 with no TAC and no shaped REQ, D2 with no resolving brief statement and no REQ/PRD/TAD) returns a `notApplicable` envelope before any check runs, which silently hides tree-wide findings. The hidden findings are real: a drafted TAD core entity is unjoined to any recordShape (R5), a registered standards pack is uncited (R7), or a `[draft]` marker sits on a TAC outside the narrowed scope (R2) even when the delta touched nothing in the stage's local scope. The pattern is the ruling, not the three instances: the review of rcf-lite PR 292 (d-2026-10-05-012, ruling R13 confirmed by Baz 2026-10-05) found three further tree-wide checks still hidden by the same short-circuit shape -- D5 `crosscut:securityArchitecture`, D5 `crosscut:operationalConcerns` and D2 `skeleton:deployAdr` -- all of which read tree-wide inputs (`tree.requirements`, `tree.userStories`, `tree.adrs`) and all of which disappear when the stage's own `reqInScope` / resolving-statement set is empty. D4 (`stories:closedSets`, `stories:ownerRefResolves` under their own `notApplicable` arm) and D6 (every check is tree-wide anyway, and the probe-ledger scan sits outside the scope early-return already) are unchanged. The fix is one shared helper the gates module applies at every stage with a tree-wide check.
decision: A stage with a tree-wide check evaluates those checks before any scope-driven `notApplicable` early-return. `src/query/gates.js` has one shared module-internal helper `treeWideFailureEnvelope(stage, gate, treeWideChecks, freezeCtx)` that takes the already-computed per-check results as `[{ name, check }]` entries and returns either `null` (every tree-wide check ok -- the stage proceeds to its own scope early-return or full checks list) or the envelope `foldState(stage, gate, checks, freezeCtx)` returns over a `checks[]` carrying the `stage:<D>:scope` placeholder plus every tree-wide check: `{ stage, gate, state: 'failing' | 'acknowledged', checks }` with no `reason` field. The helper delegates the fold to `foldState` on every stage, so a single implementation owns the acknowledgement rule and the two cannot drift: a warn-with-ack stage (D3, D5, D6) acknowledged at the current tree hash folds to `acknowledged`, and a blocking stage (D2) always folds to `failing`. The stage function computes each tree-wide check once (so the viewer and the text report render the same check object), calls the helper first when the local scope is empty, and otherwise runs its full checks list with the tree-wide check(s) interleaved in the same slot in `checks[]`. The helper governs every tree-wide check: `shapes:draftSettled` (R2), `shapes:entityJoin` (R5), `skeleton:standardsCited` (R7), and the three R13 checks `crosscut:securityArchitecture` (D5), `crosscut:operationalConcerns` (D5), `skeleton:deployAdr` (D2). It does NOT govern delta-only checks: `shapes:templateMarkers`, `shapes:pathsResolve`, `stories:closedSets`, `stories:ownerRefResolves` and the D4 floors keep running against the stage scope and continue to short-circuit on an empty scope. R2 2026-10-05 flipped `shapes:draftSettled`'s `over` label from `delta` to `tree` to match the ruling; the other six tree-wide checks already carried `over: tree`. The CHECK_PERSONA and CHECK_QUESTION fields stay fixed to their spec section 4 values.
consequences: A narrowed D2 scope that excludes every REQ/PRD/TAD/brief statement still reports an uncited standards pack through `skeleton:standardsCited` and a missing (or doubled) Deploy ADR through `skeleton:deployAdr`. A narrowed D3 scope that excludes every TAC and shaped REQ still reports a `[draft]` anywhere in the tree through `shapes:draftSettled` and an unjoined entity through `shapes:entityJoin`. A narrowed D5 scope that excludes every REQ still reports an empty `TAD.securityArchitecture` while an auth or httpApi REQ exists through `crosscut:securityArchitecture`, and an empty `TAD.operationalConcerns` while a deployed-scope AC exists through `crosscut:operationalConcerns`. The readiness compute stays pure (the helper is a function of the context, same shape as the stage functions). The `notApplicable` fold the viewer and CLI pills already read is unchanged in effect when nothing tree-wide fails. A failing envelope the helper returns carries no `reason`: the fold already lists the failing check names and the pre-R13 `reason` text (copied from the stage's `notApplicable` message) was misleading in the printed `readiness` line ('failing (no TAC ... in scope)'). The `over: tree` label flipped on `shapes:draftSettled` (R2); every other tree-wide check already carried it. Tests pin the ordering per newly governed check: a scope that excludes every item in the stage's local scope AND a tree-wide failure returns a `failing` envelope, not a `notApplicable` one.

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep the scope early-return and route tree-wide findings through D8 only
alternativesConsidered.summary: Let narrowed D2/D3/D5 scopes return `notApplicable` and surface the tree-wide failures only when D8 runs validate clean.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: D8 is the freeze gate; a narrowed scope at D2/D3/D5 is used to triage work in flight, not to freeze. Making the engineer wait until the freeze pass to see an unjoined entity, an uncited standards pack, an empty securityArchitecture or a missing Deploy ADR hides the finding during the loop that should surface it. Spec section 4 names every tree-wide check with `over: tree`; the pre-R2/R5/R7/R13 ordering contradicted that.

alternativesConsidered.name: Lift every tree-wide check to a new top-level pass before the stage dispatch
alternativesConsidered.summary: Add a `runTreeWideChecks(ctx)` compute at the readiness level that runs before every stage function and prepends its findings to the first failing stage.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Changes the readiness result shape and the viewer / CLI consumers that key off the per-stage `checks[]` array. The shared helper keeps every tree-wide check in its canonical stage so `stages[D2].checks[].name === 'skeleton:standardsCited'` still holds.

alternativesConsidered.name: Duplicate the tree-wide check into D8
alternativesConsidered.summary: Mirror `shapes:entityJoin` and `skeleton:standardsCited` into D8's checks so a narrowed D2/D3 scope's miss still gets caught at freeze.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A failing D2 at freeze fails the freeze gate anyway (D8 `freeze:priorGates`). The duplication adds a second ownership for the same check and the viewer would need to pick which name wins. The helper preserves one owning stage per tree-wide check.

alternativesConsidered.name: Limit the helper to the three checks R2/R5/R7 named and leave securityArchitecture / operationalConcerns / deployAdr behind the scope
alternativesConsidered.summary: Govern only the three checks the DEFINE step 3 spec section 18 named at R2/R5/R7 ship time and leave the three further checks the PR 292 review surfaced where they were.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The principle, not the inventory, is the ruling. Baz 2026-10-05 ratified every open ruling as recommended and confirmed R13 on the same cycle. Keeping half the tree-wide checks hidden by the scope would ship a half-fix; a narrowed D5 scope that excludes an auth REQ would still miss an empty securityArchitecture even though the whole stage computes it from the whole tree.
